structured.approach: I followed the FE-05 procedure in the frontend-steps skill and read task.code and feat.stories. I read the exact source and blast radius of renderOverdueRisk and its helpers with the codegraph MCP tool (codegraph_explore). I added node:test cases to tests/portal.test.js after the existing tests, which I did not change. There is one test for each of AC-07.1 to AC-07.10, plus the TypeError coverage cases that task.code section 6 hands over. All test data is synthetic SYN-INV data. In the AC-07.1 test, the input rows have fewer days first, the reverse of the ap_aging sort, so a re-sort inside renderOverdueRisk would fail it. I ran `node ci.mjs` from the repository root and it exited 0 (passed). I then ran `codegraph sync` and `codegraph affected`, and the only affected test file is tests/portal.test.js. Last, I wrote task.unit_tests with a table that traces each test to its acceptance criterion.

claims.text: Before FE-05, CI reported coverage 60.32, and lines 26-28 33-39 42-44 50-61 of src/ap_portal/index.js were uncovered because no test called the new functions.
The step requires unit tests that cover the new code with at least 90 percent coverage, and `node ci.mjs` must pass before the commit step.
tests/portal.test.js keeps the existing tests 'formats amounts with two decimals' and 'renders every bucket in order' unchanged, and adds tests named for AC-07.1 to AC-07.10 of renderOverdueRisk.
escapeHtml, toTwoDecimalString and riskClass each have 1 caller, inside src/ap_portal/index.js, and are reached only through the exported renderOverdueRisk.

The AC-07.1 test passes SYN-INV-001 (31 days) before SYN-INV-002 (42 days). That is the reverse of the ap_aging order (days descending), and the test expects the output in the same input order, so it shows that renderOverdueRisk keeps the given order without re-sorting.

The amount tests check that two-decimal strings, including one longer than a JS Number can hold, are shown unchanged, and that '980.5' renders as '980.50'. This follows decision D-2026-044 (Decimal, never float).

The tests assert the exact TypeError messages for a non-array rows value, a non-integer days value and an amount that is not a decimal string with at most two decimals. These are the coverage cases handed over in task.code section 6.

open_questions: Q-1 (non-blocking, Developer): feat.design B4.5 and the TRD tests T-12 to T-16 are not inputs of FE-05, so the tests are traced only to AC-07.1 to AC-07.10. Should they also be checked against B4.5?
Q-2 (non-blocking, Developer; carried from task.code Q-1): which step sets the next minor version in both index.js and package.json (TK-07.5) before FE-06?
Q-3 (non-blocking, Architect; carried from task.code Q-2): should a missing or non-string id or vendor throw TypeError? No test pins the current String(value) behaviour.
structured.summary: The STORY-07 unit tests in tests/portal.test.js cover AC-07.1 to AC-07.10 of renderOverdueRisk and the TypeError paths for rows, days and amount, using synthetic data only. The AC-07.1 test now gives the rows in the reverse of the ap_aging order, so it would catch a re-sort. `node ci.mjs` passes (exit 0), and the CI coverage gate of at least 90% is met. task.unit_tests records the tests, the trace from each test to its criterion, the CI result and the non-blocking open questions. Nothing is committed.
